Maya Chen: Heads-up — DirectHealth (insurance, enterprise) returned the vendor security questionnaire + DPA. Main asks: embeddings retention policy, data residency (EU/US), non-prod access, and SOC2 evidence for prod+staging. They requested a 30–45m enablement workshop next Wed. Attaching form: <https://redwood.internal/docs/directhealth-dpa|directhealth-dpa.pdf>

Samir Patel: On it. Quick Q — do they require BYOK/KMS? Their answers hint 'customer-managed keys preferred'. I need a list of services that touch embeddings and whether raw inputs are persisted anywhere.

Vikram Rao: If they insist on BYOK + strict isolation, Dedicated won't cut it alone — Private (VPC/on-prem) with BYOK is the usual recommendation. That changes scope/timeline (roughly 4–6 weeks for infra + key exchange).

Lina Gomez: I can run the enablement workshop and demo the embeddings retention controls. Need a 30-min slot and a sanitized sample dataset (PII/no-PII). I'll prepare an onboarding checklist and a short slide deck.

Maya Chen: I tentatively told them Wed 10–10:45am PT works. @Samir @Vikram — can you confirm coverage by EOD? They also want SOC2 evidence (data retention policy + access control screenshots) delivered before the call.

Samir Patel: Confirming I'll pull SOC2 control mapping + evidence artifacts (control IDs: CC6, CC7, RA-2 equivalent). I may need SRE to export audit logs for non-prod. Planning to drop a zip in the secure bucket.

Eric Johnson: Legal is reviewing the DPA. I'll propose a narrow BYOK clause, call out subprocessor list, and add an explicit data residency affirmation. Expect redline by tomorrow EOD. For SOC2 evidence we should provide summarized artifacts not raw logs — will propose a redacted bundle.

Maya Chen: Customer also asked about embeddings retention window and deletion guarantees for exported vectors. They want confirmation that we do not store raw customer documents after embedding generation.

Vikram Rao: Technically we persist the embeddings and a minimal metadata blob (timestamp, model version, tenancy id). Raw plaintext is not stored after processing unless the customer opted into logs. We can offer a configuration: TTL for embeddings + immediate deletion on request.

Lina Gomez: I'll add two bullets to the enablement deck: 1) Embeddings retention controls & TTL workflow, 2) BYOK key rotation flow (handshake steps).

Maya Chen: Below is a compact answers template I use for these asks — copy/paste to the Q form if helpful:

```
Q: Do you store raw inputs?
A: No — raw inputs are not persisted by default. Our inference pipeline writes only the generated embeddings and minimal metadata unless logging is explicitly enabled by the customer.

Q: Embeddings retention options?
A: Customers can choose default retention (90 days), custom TTL, or immediate deletion via API. Private deployments can set policy to never persist beyond the configured TTL.

Q: BYOK/KMS?
A: Supported on Private deployments and available as an enterprise add-on for Dedicated. We support AWS KMS and customer HSM via standard key-wrapping flows.
```

Samir Patel: Good template. I'll add control mappings and a note about where encrypted keys live.

cs-bot: Reminder: "DirectHealth DPA redline due" scheduled for 2024-07-24 16:00 PT.

Maya Chen: Next steps: (1) @Eric provide DPA redline by tomorrow, (2) @Samir bundle SOC2 evidence + control mapping, (3) @Vikram confirm infra feasibility & timeline, (4) @Lina prepare deck and request sample data. I'll confirm the workshop time with the customer once you all sign off. Thanks :pray:
